newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin summons top ministers from parliament.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin summons top ministers from parliament.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin unexpectedly summoned Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and his two first deputies to a meeting in the Kremlin, although they had been expected to spend the day in parliament.

Gennady Seleznyov, speaker of the State Duma lower house of parliament, announced the summons while Chernomyrdin was answering questions from deputies over the 1997 budget. The reason for Yeltsin's invitation was not immediately known.
Chernomyrdin told deputies he would return to parliament after seeing Yeltsin and he left for the Kremlin. First deputy premiers, reformers Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov, have also been summoned.
The government is trying to persuade the conservative Duma to agree to its proposals to cut budget spending across the board and most ministers were attending the parliament session.
A Kremlin spokesman could not say why Yeltsin wanted to see the ministers and said Yeltsin's official schedule provided only for a meeting with cellist Mstislav Rostropovich.
